utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may be seated, sir. Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Sir, can you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Milan Mandilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 9418.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be uploaded, can you tell the Court what was your profession during the war in Sarajevo between 1993 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: During the relevant period, my profession was identical to the profession that I had before that. I am a general practitioner, and then I specialised in ENT surgery. This is what I did before the war, during the war, and I continued doing that now. At the time, I was the head of the clinical department for ENT diseases.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: At the State Hospital of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Do you remember testifying before this Tribunal in the case Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic on 17 January 2007?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 9419. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are you doing with 9418?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will ask for the admission at the later stage. I will ask for the admission of both transcripts. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you also remember testifying before this Tribunal in a different case, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic case? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember testifying against General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you have an opportunity to review your testimony in both these cases?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you confirm that your previous testimony is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I will tender 65 ter numbers 9418 and 9419 into evidence. Those are the two transcripts from Dr. Mandilovic's previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 9418 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P631.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And 9419.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P632.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, did you also have an opportunity to review some of the copies of the medical records you dealt with during your testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I reviewed the medical records, and I could establish that they were valid, that they originated from two hospitals in Sarajevo, from the clinical centre and the State Hospital in Sarajevo, both of them in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 8701 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you need me to comment upon anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Just wait for the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you confirm that these are copies of authentic medical records that you signed yourself and that were issued by the State Hospital in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I can confirm this is my handwriting, and I absolutely adhere by what is stated herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is no objection, the document having been signed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P633.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we now move to 65 ter 8698. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you confirm that these are copies of authentic medical records issued by the State Hospital of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please move to page 14 of the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you confirm that this page, just in front of you, contains actually two different medical records, the one at the top being issued by the State Hospital and the other one being issued by the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this juncture, considering the fact that the Prosecutor is well aware of the fact that there are some disputes with regard to documents following, I would ask that he does not lead the witness but, rather, obtains the information from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, Your Honour, this is a 92 ter witness, and the relevant evidence about these documents are already part of the evidence before this Chamber. They are in 9418 and 9419, but considering my learned friend's objection, I will delay the discussion of this particular page to a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The point is even if they may be in evidence, if it's a disputed issue, you shouldn't lead your witness. The witness must testify, not you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. To the extent that there is an issue, I would remind my friend that we've had more than one discussion about the representations made by the Prosecution concerning these exhibits which can be found at page 582 and 583 of the transcript in the Milosevic case. So I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We are dealing with the transcript here. I think we have ruled that that is enough. The counsel has been told to ask questions and get answers and not lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, in performing your duties as a doctor with the State Hospital in Sarajevo, had you come across medical documentation issued by other Sarajevo hospitals such as the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to object to that question as also being leading because it suggests the answer, which is the basis upon which a question is determined to be leading. He can ask whether or not he came across other medical records from other hospitals in the Sarajevo region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stick to the point that the answer to these questions is already part of the trial record of this case, and I can give you the reference of the Dragomir Milosevic transcripts where the issue has been dealt with, but I'm happy to rephrase the question if that assists Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled, but let me say this to you, Mr. Cannata: This Trial Chamber is not listening to the testimony in Milosevic case. It's listening to the testimony in Perisic case. Please don't lead your witness. Ask your witness questions. That the evidence has been admitted is one thing; the other thing is that the Defence might be disputing that evidence, and, therefore, to that extent you may not lead your witness. Your witness must testify. That's what you are doing in direct examination, not you testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, I will rephrase my question, then. In performing your duties as a doctor with the State Hospital in Sarajevo, have you come across medical records issued by other Sarajevo hospitals?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And what were the other Sarajevo hospitals?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: All hospitals -- well, I came across medical documents from all hospitals, and I came across patients, naturally, who had been treated in other hospitals or checked up there, because in addition to the two hospitals we are discussing, there were other medical institutions at a lower level that were functioning in Sarajevo. We had primary health care that had been developed. First, the wounded would go to a GP for primary health care, or they would go to their military doctor at the battle-field, and then only after that they would be sent to one of the hospitals. So given my profession, I had to have constant contact with the findings from a whole series of other doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. You mentioned they will be sent to one of the hospitals. Which were the hospitals in Sarajevo that you are familiar with the medical records?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: There are two traditional hospitals, the State Hospital in Sarajevo and the clinical centre. There was an isolated hospital called the military hospital in Dobrinja because that part of Sarajevo is about 10 kilometres away. It was an independent institution, a particular institution, but given the sort of medical services it provided, I would say that this was a lower-level institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Was the clinical centre known under a different name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: No. The clinical centre was called the clinical centre, or perhaps someone else called it the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the first word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of the centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Can we go back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the first word. Can you ask the witness to please repeat himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Dr. Mandilovic, can you please repeat your answer because the interpreter couldn't catch the first word.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To make it easier to communicate, one used the term "the clinical centre," but its real name was the university clinical centre, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the State Hospital, is it just called State Hospital, nothing else? Nothing else to that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the State Hospital. Just the State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any other hospitals that you received records from, that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Documents came from health centres and, as I have already said, from hospitals that were further away. The hospital in Dobrinja, that was 10 kilometres from the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to remember the names of the hospitals that these documents came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's just the Dobrinja hospital, just the Dobrinja hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we go back to 65 ter 8698 and move to page 14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please describe what you can see in this document to the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I can see a first and last name, a patient's first and last name. This patient went to the State Hospital. I can see a registration number and the date of this visit. I can see the diagnosis, and I can see treatment prescribed, and below I can see something that is handwritten and something printed out, typed out. The patient after checkup in the State Hospital, because of the seriousness of the condition, was taken to the surgical department of the clinical centre in Sarajevo, was taken there for chest surgery, because in this finding, it quite clearly states, in the upper left-hand corner, we have the stamp of the State Hospital and the findings of the doctor, and we have the clinical centre stamp in the lower left-hand corner. Why did this happen? I wasn't there, but on the basis of the findings I can speculate as to why this was done because the first diagnosis shows that a thorax had been wounded in the State Hospital. We didn't at that time have a surgeon for such interventions and, therefore, the patient was sent by us to a higher level to see a chest surgeon in the clinical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Now, on account of your experience as a doctor with the State Hospital, are you familiar with the medical records such as the one you just saw on the screen issued by the clinical centre in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I still have the same document on the screen, the same one I had awhile ago. I don't have anything new.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: My question -- please listen carefully to my question. My question to you is --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: -- of more general terms. I'm asking you, on account of your experience as a doctor with the State Hospital, did you come across medical records issued by the clinical centre in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. May I move 65 ter 8698 into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P634.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just so I'm clear, are you moving in the entirety of that document based on the examination with regard to this one page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Guy-Smith, but why don't you stand up at the right time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, there are three reasons for that. One is that I was having a brief conversation with my assistant. The second is that it takes me longer to stand up today than it does normally, and I would not object from a sitting position because that would show the Court disrespect. If I can object immediately from a sitting position, then I will be moving that much quicker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The point regarding your very first reason, Mr. Guy-Smith, when the move was made, you were not talking. You turned after the move because I was looking at you thinking that you have anything to say about the document, and when you started talking to your colleague, that's when I admitted the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's much better. Are you tendering the entire document, sir, or 14 pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your colleague says he is tendering the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would object to the balance of the document being tendered at this point absent further foundation being laid.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, we actually discussed the very first page of this document. I'm happy to go through each single page of these documents, but the witness has reviewed these documents in the proofing session yesterday, and these documents have been reviewed by the witness again in a different proceedings and exhibited in different proceedings. These documents come as the 92 ter package of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata, will you go through the documents with the witness in this court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page of 65 ter 8698. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Is that a medical record issued by the State Hospital in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: It is. It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just ask the witness what it is. Please don't testify. Let the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. You have been warned that these documents are disputed. Let the witness testify, not you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber the hospital originating this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to tell the Court what institution originated this document? I know it's a very bad copy, but can you tell that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The Sarajevo State Hospital, you can see that in the upper left-hand corner, and down below you can see the signature of the doctor in the lower right-hand corner. This is a document issued by the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can we move to the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, once again --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just wait for my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Again, sir, can you tell us, what's the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Dr. Mandilovic -- actually, can we please move to the next page. Hold on one second. Thank you, sir. Can you please testify to the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can we please move to the next document, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Mandilovic. Again, please wait for my question before answering. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what the source of this document is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is also a medical document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the source of this document for the Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could I know what page we are on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: The one I just called, and it's been uploaded on e-court, it's 0036-0193.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's the one that's signed by Dr. Dzafic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I can only tell it's 0036-0193. It should be page 9 as it appears on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand the previous one was signed by Dr. Dzafic. This one has an illegible signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I don't understand the point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your colleague is saying that the previous one was signed by Dr. Dzafic and this one has got an illegible signature. That's what he says. I guess he is asking you to go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm just -- I'm trying to figure out where the previous page because when we get up to the -- when we finish with this examination, the issue comes up once again with regard to the admission of his exhibit, I want to make sure that I can reference the specific page, and since I have a signature here of Dr. Dzavic, I want to make sure that when I'm discussing the matter with the Court I'm discussing the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we please go back to the page number 8. If I can assist the Defence counsel, is that the page he is talking about because, really, I don't understand what page are we talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: The witness already testified to this page, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead. Go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move to the next page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Mandilovic, can you tell us what is the source of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a medical document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Court the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a medical document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Your Honours, may I have one minute to consult with my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a medical document from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Again, sir, can you tell us the source of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yet again, it's from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Next document, please. 0036-0197.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This medical document comes from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what the source of this document is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This medical document also originates in the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. And how can you make that conclusion? On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: In the case of all these documents, and that includes the last one that we have on the screen now, there are three elements that lead me to this conclusion. There's the heading where it says the State Hospital Sarajevo in the upper left-hand side corner; then we have the stamp of the State Hospital in Sarajevo; and we have the signature of the manager of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next document, please. Your Honours, I take that we already discussed the document. I'm happy to ask again questions to the witness, but I take this is already evidence, that the evidence of the witness is already recorded for these documents. Can we move to the next one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what is the source of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The State Hospital in Sarajevo is the source of this document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we please move to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you tell me what is the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This medical document originates from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move to what should be the last page, the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you tell us the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The source of this medical document is the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, finally, to the last document of this exhibit, can we move to the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us the source of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This document also originates from the Sarajevo State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Mandilovic. Your Honours, at this moment I will tender this document into an exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The documents are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, they were already given P634, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might need to seek your guidance because this is -- I think it might be a required exercise, but I have a number of documents. Now, if the Chamber's position is that the witness go through each single record, then it might take a little bit longer than the time estimated -- the Prosecution has expected for this witness. I'm at your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You unfortunately don't get guidance from the Bench on how you prosecute your case. The Bench intervenes as and when your colleague rises to object and deals with that situation at that time according to how the Bench sees the situation. So we can't give you guidance on what to do, really. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might be of some assistance because I certainly don't want to waste court time. That's not what my intent is here. So with regard to the balance of the documents that I believe the Prosecution intends to proffer through this witness, I believe if the Prosecution can engage in some prefatory questioning of the witness with regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, may I interrupt you. Let the Prosecution deal with its case, and you rise up when you have to rise up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't tell him how to run his case. Let him run his case the way he wants to run his case. Mr. Cannata, may you proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Can I have 65 ter 8692 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This medical document originates from the clinical centre of the university in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And now can you tell the origin of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The origin of this document is the clinical centre of the university in Sarajevo, to be more specific, from the department of trauma or trauma centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asking the question a second time, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sorry. It's a mis-catch in the record. I said -- my question was how, how can you tell the origin of this document. It's a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell on the basis of the facsimile that we see in the right-hand corner and, also, the signature of the doctor who signed the medical document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: On account of your service with the State Hospital, how many medical records have you had an opportunity to come across issued by the clinical centre of the university in Sarajevo, roughly speaking, of course?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you a number. However, there were many such occasions. Patients came to both hospitals for checkups, and it often happened that due to the major shelling of the town and the general alert that had been sound, the patients couldn't choose where to come for checkups. There were often situations that they started being treated at one hospital and finished their treatment in the other due to their inability to move about the town at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And when a patient from the clinical centre came to the State Hospital, was treated -- sorry, let me strike this, and I'll rephrase the question. The question will be, when a patient from the clinical centre came to the State Hospital, did you receive the medical file issued and prepared by the clinical centre? Did you have an opportunity to review that file, those medical records?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. Every patient is issued with their medical documents, and when they present themselves to a different medical institution, they have to present their medical documentation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a number of 65 ters that deal with medical records issued by the clinical centre. I'm going to ask the witness to review, with your leave, the first page of these documents and ask for the admission, unless there's any objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asking a very difficult question, sir. An objection will come when you get to an objectionable stage. Just carry on, just prosecute your case and --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. Can we ask 86 -- actually, can we go back to 8692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't this 8692 that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's on the screen, and I will ask for its admission into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to 65 ter 8692, to the extent that the document is being offered through this witness as an accurate reflection of records, there is no objection. To the extent this document is being offered with regard to the truth of the contents that is contained within these records, there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours. Yes, the Prosecution position is that Dr. Mandilovic is for these documents entitled to speak only to the -- to attest the accuracy and the validity and the fact that the documents, the medical records are authentic copies issued by the clinical centre. He will not give evidence as to the contents of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understanding that they are not being offered for that purpose, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P635.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we please have 8693 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court its source?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This document originates from the clinical centre in Sarajevo, to be more precise, from the orthopaedic ward.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can this document be exhibited, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If this document is being proposed under the same conditions as last document, there is no objection. Once again, not to speak the truth of the contents contained in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P636.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to 65 ter 8694. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell us its source?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: The source of this document is the clinical centre of the university in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, can this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Under the same conditions, no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, under the same conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if we clarify that so that we don't have Mr. Guy-Smith standing up every time. He says he's got difficulty standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. If that may assist, I can anticipate that the following 65 ter numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are admitted for that purpose, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. So let's give this one an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 8694 will be Exhibit P637, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And the next 65 ter numbers will be under the same conditions tendering into evidence are 8695, 8696, 8697, 8699, 8700, 8702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you tendering them?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I tender these documents into evidence, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those documents are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 8695 will be Exhibit P638; 65 ter 8696 will be Exhibit P639; 65 ter 8697 will be Exhibit P640; 65 ter 8699 will be Exhibit P641; 65 ter 8700 will be Exhibit P642; and 65 ter 8702 will be Exhibit P643.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, can we please have 65 ter 8703 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Dr. Mandilovic, let me ask you this: How long have you been a medical doctor?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Almost 30 years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, in performing your duties as a doctor, have you come across forensic reports issued by the Forensic Institute of the Faculty of Medicine in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what this document is?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: This document is an excerpt from the protocol of the Forensic Institute of the School of Medicine in Sarajevo. It's an autopsy report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us how can you establish that it actually originates from the Forensic Institute of Medicine in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Because I can see in the left upper corner the name of the faculty of medicine, the forensic institute, the date, and in the right-hand corner I can see the signature of the forensic specialist who is a pathologist and also a professor of the School of Medicine of the University of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Throughout your experience as a doctor with the State Hospital, have you come across similar documents to this one?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MANDILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will move this document into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With the same condition as the previous documents, there would be no objection, which is that he is not -- these documents are not being offered for the truth of the contents contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Same conditions as before, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have an Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P644, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the clock, and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it then be a convenient time to take the break. Doctor, I'm sorry to do this to you. This is the end of the day for this court, so we'll have to continue tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. You are warned not to discuss the case with anybody now that you are still in the witness box, not even with your lawyer, until you have finished testifying. The case stands adjourned to tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom II. Court adjourned.
